beats.text: The first misconception to retire is that lipid metabolism in cancer is about energy storage. In a proliferating cancer cell, lipids are primarily structural and signaling molecules , membrane phospholipids, cholesterol, and the lipid anchors that hold proteins like RAS at the plasma membrane. When a cell divides, it must double its membranes. That requires fat. And many cancer cells, unlike most quiescent adult tissue, build their own rather than importing what they need. Most differentiated cells take up fatty acids from the circulation.

beats.text: Many cancers cannot survive without a steady supply of glutamine , the most abundant amino acid in blood , even when glucose is plentiful. This is the second major metabolic axis, and it is worth understanding not just as "another nutrient" but as something that does four distinct jobs simultaneously. After import through transporters such as ASCT2 (SLC1A5), glutaminase converts glutamine to glutamate, which is then converted to alpha-ketoglutarate and fed into the citric acid cycle. beats.text: The most elegant metabolic dependency story currently in clinical development involves not a pathway the cancer actively upregulates but a gap it cannot fill , and a second vulnerability that gap quietly creates. MTAP (methylthioadenosine phosphorylase) sits on chromosome 9p21, directly beside the tumor suppressor CDKN2A. When CDKN2A is deleted , as it is in roughly 30 percent of all human cancers , MTAP is frequently co-deleted as a bystander, with no selective pressure for or against its loss.

title: THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT AS
A METABOLIC ECOSYSTEM.
segments.body_html: Hypoxia.→Acidosis.→Nutrient depletion.→Lactate as an immunosuppressive signal.→Stromal metabolic exchange.

beats.text: A tumor is not a uniform mass of identical cancer cells. It is a spatially heterogeneous ecosystem , cancer cells, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, macrophages, T cells, NK cells, and extracellular matrix, all coexisting in a metabolic environment that no healthy tissue would produce. Hypoxia. Tumors outgrow their blood supply, and their interior oxygen levels are typically far below normal tissue values. Hypoxic regions are also radioresistant , radiation kills largely through reactive oxygen species, and without oxygen the chemistry is blunted.

beats.text: How much dietary metabolic intervention actually does in patients , whether caloric restriction, ketogenic diet, or methionine restriction can meaningfully starve tumors in humans, as opposed to in mice , is unresolved. The preclinical signals are strong; the clinical evidence is weak and hard to obtain rigorously. Whether metabolic and immune combination strategies can be made to work reliably is open. The rationale is mechanistically clear: relieve the metabolic suppression of T cells, then release the checkpoint brakes.
